newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo says chairman resigns over copper loss.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo says chairman resigns over copper loss.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Wednesday that its chairman Tomiichi Akiyama had resigned from his posts as chairman and member of the board of directors due to the trading house's $2.6 billion loss in the copper market.
It added that he had been appointed an adviser to the company.

The company said that Akiyama, who was president of the company when it first announced its copper market losses in June 1996, resigned "in order to put the matter behind (us)". He was later made chairman in a previously scheduled management change.
Sumitomo also said its management was not involved in the copper trading responsible for the losses, which it blamed on its former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.

Akiyama said in a statement that, "While I knew nothing about Mr. Hamanaka's hidden trading, I was the president of the corporation when much of the trading occurred." Hamanaka, who was fired last June, pleaded guilty in a Tokyo court last week to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with the losses.

Regarding the timing of Akiyama's resignation, Sumitomo said he had decided last June to resign as soon as possible, although he remained in the post until now to offer support as his successor to the presidency sought to deal with the aftermath of the scandal.
